summary: Correction to attempt 1's malformed report: the required top-level `summary` field is now present and the full report is reproduced; the implementation itself was verified unmodified in the worktree (uncommitted changes: src/app.rs +1, src/ui/layout.rs +2, src/app/root.rs +245, new src/app/spawn.rs; no commits by this agent; Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock byte-identical; stale prior-run dotfile removed to keep the change set clean). Delivered per ticket: the Workspace menu gains 'Open workspace' immediately above 'Disconnect' (label exact, deliberately ungated during busy turns); its arm calls PacketApp::open_workspace(), which resolves the running binary via resolve_self_executable (or the #[cfg(test)-only seam, None in shipping code), calls spawn_sibling — Stdio::null on all three streams, whole inherited environment, Child dropped immediately so the parent never holds, polls, or reaps the sibling — and pushes an info toast ('Opening a new Packet window') or a path-embedding warning toast; it mutates no screen, dialog, draft, queue, synthesis, or cancellation state. Fresh gate evidence on the pinned rustc/cargo 1.98.1: full `cargo test` rc=0 (407 lib + 2 integration passed, 0 failed, 1 opt-in ignored), `cargo test --lib app::spawn` 4/4, `cargo test --lib open_workspace` 2/2, manifest diff empty, change-set containment diff exact, no `env_clear` in spawn code, main.rs arg-blind, and clippy --all-targets strict parity versus a shadow expansion of HEAD (112==112 sorted warnings, empty diff, 0 naming any new symbol). Residual caveat, disclosed: the terminal native two-window demonstration requires a display, which this headless container lacks; every mechanism feeding it (zero-args spawn, arg-blind main, Welcome-default screen, wholesale env inheritance, no-touch contract, failure+retry path) is automated-tested.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given a connected window mid-way through a planner turn (status line reads '● Working'), when the operator opens Workspace and clicks 'Open workspace', then a second Packet window appears presenting the initial screen (path field, Open button) within a couple of seconds, and the first window's turn keeps advancing with no 'Turn aborted' toast and no change to its draft or status.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Covered automatably end to end except the final pixel-level window appearance: `cargo test --lib open_workspace` (2 passed, 0 failed) drives the real Workspace menu click into 'Open workspace' with a genuinely hanging turn (whose worker sleeps until canceled) and asserts the 'Opening a new Packet window' toast is painted, no 'Turn aborted' text appears, screen stays Connected, and the turn keeps its registered controller. Initial-screen landing is proven mechanically rather than visually: `src/main.rs` inspects no argv (grep for `env::args` finds nothing, asserted by a gate command), the sibling is launched with zero arguments (`Command::new(bin)` with no args in `spawn_sibling`), `PacketApp::default()` initializes `screen: Screen::Welcome` (src/app/root.rs), and the environment-inheritance unit test proves the sibling sees the parent's whole environment. Limitation stated plainly: this headless container has no display server, so the two simultaneous native windows themselves are the remaining manual mile, exercisable via the checklist from the prior run (cargo run on a display-connected host mid-turn, Workspace > 'Open workspace', expect second window on Welcome while the first keeps 'Working'; kill either, the other survives).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given the same connected window, when 'Open workspace' is clicked, then the invoking window's active turn, active implementations, queue and draft are unchanged in state (observably: no cancel requests issued, screen still Connected, composer draft text identical), because the new handler touches none of those fields.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Met by direct assertion, not inference: `open_workspace_spawns_a_detached_sibling_without_touching_the_session` prescreens a fake in-flight state (live `TurnController` backed by a harness that hangs until canceled, an idle `Controller::idle_fixture()` in `active_implementations`, and an unsent composer draft), performs two consecutive menu clicks, and asserts after each: `Arc::ptr_eq` of the still-registered active turn, `cancel_requested() == false` on the turn, `cancellation_requested() == false` on the active implementation, `chat_draft()` byte-identical to pre-click, and `matches!(screen, Connected)`. The handler itself (`PacketApp::open_workspace`, src/app/root.rs:1297) touches only `toasts` (info/warning) and performs the spawn — no `request_cancel`, no `screen`/`dialog`/`synch`/`queue` mutation, documented in-line as the contract contrast with `disconnect()`.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given an environment started with PACKET_HOME=<scratch-dir> and PACKET_PI_BIN=<custom path>, when 'Open workspace' spawns a sibling, then the sibling reads the same overridden home and harness binary (observable: its session state lands under <scratch-dir> and its harness discovery probes the custom binary), because the spawn copies no environment deliberately — it inherits wholesale.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: Proven by a real subprocess: `app::spawn::tests::spawn_sibling_inherits_the_parent_environment_wholesale` spawns a probe script THROUGH `spawn_sibling`, the child records the parent-visible variable it received to a fresh file, and the test asserts the round-tripped value equals the parent's exactly — demonstrating that variables already held by the launching process travel intact through the wholesale-inheriting environment that `PACKET_HOME`, `PACKET_TURN_TIMEOUT_SECS` and `PACKET_PI_BIN` occupy (none of which the spawn touches, reads, or re-sets). Complementing static gate: a comment-stripped grep asserts there is NO `env_clear` call site in src/app/spawn.rs (rc=0). All four spawn unit tests pass: `cargo test --lib app::spawn` rc=0.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given the spawn fails (simulated in tests by pointing the seam at a nonexistent binary; in practice a deleted/moved executable), when 'Open workspace' is clicked, then a warning toast appears embedding the failing binary path or IO error, the menu closed cleanly, the screen stays Connected, and no partially-started zombie interaction occurs; clicking again retries identically.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: `open_workspace_spawn_failure_warns_with_path_and_leaves_the_session_usable` points the test seam at a nonexistent binary, clicks 'Open workspace', and asserts: a warning paints the failing-path token, no success toast fires, screen remains Connected, the draft string is intact; it then clicks a SECOND time and asserts the identical graceful failure repeats (repeat-request stability, no zombie half-interaction). Module level: `spawn_sibling_missing_binary_reports_failure_with_the_path_embedded` asserts the Err string embeds '/nonexistent/packet-sibling-bin' and the call returns in well under 2 s (no hang, no panic — the whole suite is green). Menu closure after the click is the shared `s.on_header_action(action); ui.close();` loop every sibling menu entry uses (src/ui/layout.rs).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given two sibling windows both connected to the SAME repository, when both persist chat or contended for the implementation queue, then no corrupt interleaved file bytes appear (atomic rename-swap writes win whole) and queue access serializes through the existing filesystem lock — no crash, no lost-update corruption beyond last-whole-write-wins.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: This ticket adds no cross-process memory or new locking — the sibling is a separate OS process, and the gate-asserted change set is exactly {src/app.rs, src/app/root.rs, src/ui/layout.rs} + new src/app/spawn.rs, so the two same-repo defenses are the PRE-EXISTING primitives, byte-untouched here and still green: per-slug chat persistence under $PACKET_HOME writes exclusively through `crate::artifacts::atomic_write` (rename-swap; `persistence::chat_store::tests::append_then_load_round_trips` and `torn_trailing_line_is_skipped_not_fatal` pass via `cargo test --lib chat_store`, rc=0), and implementation-queue contention serializes through `implementation_queue::acquire`'s inter-process flock `try_lock` on `packet-queue.lock` (src/core/implementation_queue.rs:64) whose stock error text already anticipates this scenario: 'Auto queue is already running in another Packet window'. Whole-file last-write-wins is the established NFR-2 semantic; no weaker path is introduced.
